perspective:
From Harold’s subjective perspective, he has access to:

- He is a project manager whose project team seems unmotivated and whose progress is suffering. He feels frustrated and anxious, so he seeks advice from Arthur, his friend/advisor, at a coffee shop.
- Harold tells Arthur that his team seems completely unmotivated and it is affecting progress; he is at his wits’ end.
- He hears Arthur advise him to understand what drives each team member individually, try one-on-one conversations, and help people feel valued and understood personally.
- Harold decides to try Arthur’s advice and feels hopeful and relieved.
- In a team meeting, Harold says he wants one-on-one chats to understand what motivates each person and believes this will help them work better together. He hears Team Member 1 say it could be helpful and Team Member 2 say they are open to it. Harold says he will schedule time and wants the project to succeed together.
- Later, Harold observes that the team still is not responding well. He feels disappointed and worried, and he tells Arthur that the suggestions did not work.
- He hears Arthur suggest there may be deeper issues: personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper.
- Harold decides to hold another round of one-on-one meetings to investigate team dynamics.
- In those meetings, Harold asks for concerns or problems. He hears Team Member 1 say there is tension between a few team members affecting work. Harold says he will look into resolving conflicts. He hears Team Member 2 say they feel overwhelmed by the workload and stressed. Harold says he will see if tasks can be redistributed and that their well-being is important.
- Harold feels optimistic and empowered. He believes addressing individual concerns will improve team performance and intends to create a more supportive, open team environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities.
- Harold announces these changes to the team. He hears Team Member 1 say it sounds great and will help, and Team Member 2 agree that it is good their concerns are being addressed. Harold says he is glad and emphasizes that their input and well-being are crucial.

Harold does not have access to Arthur’s or the team members’ unspoken thoughts, narrator-only labels about them, or events he did not observe or hear.
